h: From the river to the Science Maze
p: Turbinia may grab the headlines, but there's a lot more here once you start exploring. The Story of the Tyne gallery takes you along the river through the centuries, showing how one stretch of water shaped the coal trade, the shipyards and the people who lived and worked alongside it. It's a great primer before you head down to the Quayside and look at the bridges with fresh eyes.

Younger visitors tend to make a beeline for the Science Maze, where puzzles, gadgets and hands-on experiments make the big ideas feel like play. Other galleries look at working lives on Tyneside and at the many people who have made the region their home over the years, which gives a good balance of science and social history.

Entry is free, so it's a brilliant one for a family on a budget, and it's easy to come back for a second go rather than cramming everything into one day. The building also houses Tyne and Wear Archives, a handy one for anyone digging into local family history, though you'll want to look into how that works before turning up.

From Blandford Square you're within a few minutes' walk of some of Newcastle's best bits. The Centre for Life sits near Central Station if the kids still have energy for more science, Chinatown on Stowell Street is close for a bite to eat, and St James' Park looms over that side of the city centre. The Castle Keep and Black Gate, which gave the city its name, are just beyond the station too.
